label: Heavy going
summary: A Sunday of war and one shared celebration leaves the world at 38, still in the 'Bad' band. US Central Command ran a ninth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, with explosions reported in Tabriz, Bushehr, Chabahar, Konarak, Bandar Mahshahr, Bandar Imam Khomeini, Jask and Sirik, and among the targets the part-built Darkhovin nuclear plant in Khuzestan, which the IAEA says held no nuclear material; Iran fired back at three Arab states hosting American forces, setting a Kuwaiti power and desalination plant ablaze for a second straight day in a country that draws about 90 percent of its drinking water from desalination, while Jordan said it downed three of four incoming missiles and Bahrain said it thwarted an attack. An American service member was killed in northern Iraq, the seventeenth US death of the conflict. The clearest counterweight came from Washington, where Secretary of State Marco Rubio said diplomatic solutions remain on the table if Iran stops attacking Strait of Hormuz shipping, and described a growing split in Tehran between militants and those prioritising economic recovery. Ukraine absorbed the largest ballistic missile barrage on Kyiv of the entire war: 41 missiles and 125 drones nationwide, one killed and 16 wounded in the capital and roughly a dozen more dead from Kharkiv to Odesa, with Zelensky again pleading for interceptors. Elsewhere the ledger was grim: about 50 Malian soldiers were killed in an FLA and JNIM ambush on a convoy leaving Anefis; the Syrian Observatory put the toll from clashes between Damascus and the SDF at 530, including 76 civilians; DR Congo's Ebola epidemic reached 2,423 confirmed cases and 967 deaths, prompting Canada to bar entry to foreign nationals recently in the DRC against UN advice. The Americas took two disasters, a shallow magnitude-5.1 quake in Peru's Junin region that killed five and displaced more than 300, and the capsizing of the ferry MV Barima in Guyana with 66 people missing, while Europe's heat kept accumulating, Germany alone at roughly 9,800 heat-related deaths. Against that, two genuine highs: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time at MetLife Stadium to win the World Cup before a global audience, and Harvard mathematician Levent Alpoge announced an AI-assisted counterexample disproving the 87-year-old Jacobian conjecture, described by peers as the hardest mathematical problem yet cracked with AI help and verified within a day. The headline matches the rubric formula with no adjustment.

drivers.headline: US Central Command launches a ninth consecutive evening of strikes on Iran, hitting military command centres, air defence and coastal surveillance sites, maritime capabilities and missile and drone launch sites in an effort to break Tehran's ability to close the Strait of Hormuz; explosions are reported in Tabriz, Bushehr, Chabahar and Konarak on the Gulf of Oman, Bandar Mahshahr and Bandar Imam Khomeini on the Persian Gulf and Jask and Sirik on the strait itself, with the part-built Darkhovin nuclear plant in Khuzestan among the targets

Iran fires drones and missiles at three Arab states hosting US forces, setting a Kuwaiti power and water desalination plant ablaze for the second day running in a country that draws roughly 90 percent of its drinking water from desalination; Jordan says it shot down three of four incoming missiles and Bahrain says it thwarted attacks, while Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi calls the American strike on the Darkhovin nuclear site a 'dangerous assault' on civilian infrastructure and pledges a response

A US service member is killed and another wounded in northern Iraq during a controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone, bringing American deaths in the conflict to 17; the same day eight Iranian Kurdish opposition fighters are wounded in a drone strike near Erbil and Israeli interceptors are fired over Eilat as Iranian missiles target nearby Aqaba in Jordan

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio says diplomatic solutions remain on the table if Iran stops attacking shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, insisting any agreement 'has to be real, it has to be a deal that they're willing to live by', and describes a growing split inside Iran between militant factions and those prioritising economic recovery that he says could become 'a very positive development'; Oman, Qatar, Pakistan and Egypt continue to push a proposed pause built on the Muscat talks

Russia launches the largest ballistic missile attack on Kyiv since the start of the full-scale war, firing 41 missiles including 25 ballistic and 125 attack drones across Ukraine from about 1:30am; one person is killed and 16 wounded in the capital with fires in the Sviatoshynskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Solomyanskyi, Desnianskyi and Dnipro districts, and a dozen more are killed from Kharkiv to Odesa, as Zelensky calls protection against ballistic missiles Ukraine's top priority amid a shortage of Patriot interceptors

At least 50 Malian soldiers are killed when an army convoy leaving the strategic northern town of Anefis is ambushed by the Tuareg separatist Azawad Liberation Front and the al-Qaeda-linked JNIM, both of which claim the attack; the assault follows weeks of heavy fighting for Anefis, which the two groups briefly seized in early July while besieging a base holding Malian troops and Russian Africa Corps paramilitaries

DR Congo's Bundibugyo-virus Ebola epidemic reaches 2,423 confirmed cases, 967 deaths and 469 recoveries, the fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record, with Ituri province accounting for more than 90 percent of cases and 80 percent of deaths and no approved vaccine or treatment available; Canada responds by temporarily barring entry to foreign nationals who have recently been in the DRC, a measure that runs against UN and WHO guidance on travel restrictions

A shallow magnitude-5.1 earthquake centred on Chongos Bajo in Peru's Chupaca province, Junin region, kills at least five people, injures more than 30 and leaves over 300 displaced, with most deaths in the Pumpunya sector where adobe and quincha houses collapsed; the national civil defence institute blames the 24-kilometre depth combined with fragile traditional construction, and authorities weigh declaring a state of emergency as power cuts hit Sapallanga and Chilca

The ferry MV Barima capsizes in Guyana with 66 people reported missing and 67 rescued, triggering a large search-and-rescue operation on one of the country's river routes and adding a second mass-casualty disaster to the Americas on the same weekend as the Peruvian earthquake

Europe's record summer heat keeps compounding: by 19 July Germany alone is estimated to have suffered roughly 9,800 heat-related deaths across the season's successive heat domes, with its lifeguard federation reporting close to 100 drowning deaths, extreme marine heatwaves recorded in the North Sea and English Channel, and wildfires burning through southern France, Spain, Portugal and Greece after a run of national temperature records

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey to win the 2026 FIFA World Cup, Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute after Enzo Fernandez was sent off in stoppage time; Rodri takes the Golden Ball, Luis de la Fuente becomes the oldest World Cup-winning manager at 65, and Spain becomes the first country to hold the men's and women's World Cups at the same time, in a final watched by a global audience of hundreds of millions

Harvard mathematician Levent Alpoge announces a counterexample disproving the Jacobian conjecture in dimensions greater than two, an 87-year-old problem posed by Ott-Heinrich Keller in 1939 and listed by Stephen Smale among the great unsolved problems of the 21st century; the work was done with substantial help from an AI model and the 216-character counterexample was independently verified within a day, with researchers calling it the most difficult mathematical problem yet cracked with AI assistance
